questions.question: Iris walks 1 miles in the morning and 2,640 feet in the afternoon. How many feet does she walk altogether?
questions.hint: 1 mile = 5,280 feet. Convert the morning walk, then add the afternoon walk.

questions.question: Zoe has a ribbon 3 yards long. She cuts off 18 inches. How many inches remain?
questions.hint: 1 yard = 3 feet = 36 inches. Convert the whole ribbon, then subtract the piece cut off.

questions.question: A bag holds 2 pounds of flour. Iris uses 12 ounces. How many ounces of flour remain?
questions.hint: 1 pound = 16 ounces. Find the starting weight in ounces, then subtract 12.

questions.question: Zoe fills 2 one-gallon pitchers with lemonade. Each serving is 2 cups. How many servings can she pour?
questions.hint: 1 US gallon = 4 quarts = 16 cups. Convert to cups, then divide by 2 cups per serving.

questions.question: Each of 3 bottles holds 1 pint of water. How many US fluid ounces do the bottles hold altogether?
questions.hint: 1 US pint = 2 cups and 1 cup = 8 US fluid ounces. Find the amount per bottle, then multiply.

questions.question: A recipe uses 3 tablespoons of oil per batch. Iris makes 2 batches. How many teaspoons of oil does she need?
questions.hint: 1 tablespoon = 3 teaspoons. Find the teaspoons for one batch, then multiply by the number of batches.

questions.question: Zoe has 2 quarts of juice. She pours out 3 cups. How many cups are left?
questions.hint: 1 US quart = 2 pints = 4 cups. Convert to cups before subtracting.

questions.question: A shelf can hold 10 pounds. There are already 1 pounds of books on it. Each new book weighs 8 ounces. How many new books can be added without going over the limit?
questions.hint: Subtract the existing weight from 10 pounds. Convert the remaining capacity to ounces, then divide by 8.

questions.question: Iris has a rope 4 feet long. She cuts it into pieces that are 6 inches long. How many complete pieces can she make?
questions.hint: 1 foot = 12 inches. Convert the rope length to inches, then divide by 6.

questions.question: Zoe needs 2 cups of milk. Her measuring spoon holds 2 tablespoons. How many full spoonfuls does she need?
questions.hint: 1 US cup = 16 tablespoons. Find the total tablespoons, then divide by 2.
